summary: The big news is bad: the live Lined-up buys list has now closed 41 trades and every one was stopped at -1R (11 on the entry day). All filled trades, open ones included, average -0.74R, against a +0.84R backtest. That trips the kill rule we set last week. New research this week (pairs version of 'the trade', the ratio watch, IPO supply) is promising but none of it reaches t 2. Nothing from last week's plan was built, and the playbook still says 'Press, size up' 26 sessions after two shallow thrusts while breadth has been Weak. Best next step: switch the Lined-up card to 'hold off' and find out why live fills lose when the backtest won (#1). Then split the post-thrust state into deep vs shallow (#2).

items.title: Lined-up buys: kill rule hit. Switch the card to 'hold off' and audit live fills against the backtest
items.where: lifecycle layer (lineupCard gate, data/lineup_ledger.csv, lined-up hourly alerts)
items.how: Ledger Oct 26 to Nov 20: 54 filled, 41 stopped at -1R (11 on entry day), 13 open with +1.3R between them, so -0.74R a trade vs +0.84R backtested. Quiet build is worse (-0.92R) than Blossom (-0.63R). Last week's rule said 30 closed trades with average R under 0 means 'hold off', so the first step is to put the card and the alerts in hold-off mode and keep logging. Then replay the ledger's exact signals through the backtest code: same trigger, same fill (max of open and trigger), same stop (dip-day low), same days. That tells us whether the gap comes from the code (fill or stop handled…
items.test: Kill rule already met (41 closed, all -1R). Audit: the backtest's same-day stop rate and average R on these same 102 signals. If the backtest also loses on them, it's the market, and the gate should require strong or post-deep-thrust breadth. If the backtest wins on them, the live fill or stop code is wrong: fix it and re-run the 2-year backtest.
items.kill: Re-enable only once the fixed rule is positive on the backtest in both halves (t 2+) AND ex-post on these 102 ledger signals is no worse than -0.2R. Otherwise retire the buy list and keep the lifecycle stages as information only.

items.title: Post-thrust playbook: split deep vs shallow thrusts before saying 'Press'
items.where: playbook_state (playbook.py 'thrust' state advice + setup verdicts); washout_thrust card
items.how: Carried over for the second week. Today the playbook reads 'Post-thrust, Press, size up' at 26 sessions in, while the Reviewer flags Weak breadth for 3+ sessions and ATH Magnet, Leader Pullback and VCP slumping (-0.20 to -0.27R). Round Number is Focus but -0.13R over the last 30 sessions. Both recent thrusts were shallow (Oct 15: SPY -2%; Nov 4: -3.5%). Their high-beta lists did -20% and -6% vs the market, while the deep ones (Apr 2025, Mar 2026) did +26% and +34%. Split the state into post-thrust deep and shallow. A shallow thrust gets 'Selective, normal size' and also leaves the thrust…
items.test: trade_bt by state, re-cut by thrust depth (deep = SPY pullback 8%+ and T2108 25 or under), clustered per thrust, both halves; confirm on the 11-year warehouse (#3), where there are many more thrusts. Build if shallow post-thrust R is below deep by t 2+ with the same sign in both halves.
items.kill: Shallow and deep within 0.1R of each other, or the halves disagree: keep one post-thrust state.

items.title: Re-test the core edges on 11 years (warehouse step 2), now including the lined-up dip rule and supply breaks
items.where: tools/warehouse (11-year Yahoo data on branch warehouse-data); later a stacked-R line on launchPicksCard and lineupCard
items.how: Third week carried over. The lined-up failure (#1) is the clearest sign yet that edges found on about 2 bull-heavy years with 2 deep thrusts can vanish live. Put the lined-up dip, the supply-break hold (top-20% groups +0.48R, t 2.3), box longs in leading groups and the post-thrust window into the 11-year warehouse with fixed columns: thrust depth, leading group, lifecycle BUY, SPY above its 50-day, breadth state. Only lifts that survive go into a stacked expected R.
items.test: Pre-register the columns (grade 85%+ before looking at outcomes). For each lift: R with minus R without, per date, clustered by month, t 2+, same sign in both halves AND before 2024 vs 2024 onward. Score the stacked R on the later half only: top fifth minus bottom fifth above 0 and rank IC 0.05+.
items.kill: Post-thrust or leading-group lift about 0 before 2024: drop it from the grades and say so on the cards. Stacked R IC under 0.05: show proven single tags only.

items.title: Launch picks: at most one open pick per sub-theme
items.where: launch.select (skip sub-themes already held) and launch.replay
items.how: Worse again this week. Friday's list adds EPAM, the 5th IT Services pick in 5 weeks (IT -14%, CTSH -2% stopped, CDW +11%, ACN -5% vs SPY), and IOT, the 3rd Enterprise SaaS pick. The 12 entered picks average about -3.5% vs SPY and 4 are stopped. They are early in 13-week holds, so this is not a verdict, but the concentration is a risk. Skip a sub-theme that already has an open pick (or cap it at 2) and take the next name.
items.test: launch.replay both ways on every past week: 13-week return vs SPY, worst open-book drawdown, t in both halves. Build if the average is the same or better (within 1 pt) and the worst drawdown is smaller.
items.kill: Average falls more than 1 pt vs SPY or a half turns negative: keep the current rule (sticking with the leading group may be the edge).

items.title: 'The trade' as a pair, only when the winners hold up
items.where: the_trade layer (info card); possible context line on Breadth next to ratio_watch
items.how: New card: long the winning fifth of sub-themes and short the losing fifth, picked with no hindsight, made +3.5% over 20 sessions (+2.8% on independent windows, t 1.2; worst -22.8%). Separately, winners that hold up on the losers' best days were +1.1% (t 2.0, both halves). Combine the two: enter the pair only when the winners are holding up, and test the long leg alone too, since short junk baskets carry squeeze risk. Also add the ratio watch (RSP/SPY, MAGS/SOXX tiers) as columns on the same test, so it gets a real test instead of sitting as an info tile.
items.test: Signals from data up to the entry day, next-open entry, 10 and 20 sessions, non-overlapping windows, t 2+ with the same sign in both halves; report the long-only leg and the worst window. Redo on the 11-year warehouse once #3 exists.
items.kill: The hold-up condition adds less than +1 pt to the pair, or t stays under 2: keep it as an info card and stop re-testing.

items.title: Agent layers and the IPO-supply forward test: wait
items.where: decision_log (catalyst, calendar, macro_brief); Trade Story ipo-supply-anthropic
items.how: 474 settled ideas but only 21 dates. Closest is macro tailwind at t 1.85, but its halves differ a lot (+0.6 / +8.3 pts) and the code backtest says no edge (t 0.35 on 6,783 signals), so it's probably noise. brief_low_risk still has 0 'low' rows: the macro brief's risk field never changes, so it can't be tested without a relative scale (that would be an agent prompt change, Adam's call). The IPO-supply study settles around Dec 17 (20 sessions after the Nov 18 pricing).
items.test: t 2+ over 20+ dates with the same sign in both halves. IPO: AI hardware and crowded winners vs SPY at +5 and +20 sessions after pricing, compared with the SpaceX case (-13% at 20d).
items.kill: No agent layer at |t| 1+ after ~100 more settled ideas: cut the catalyst agent to earnings-date checks only. IPO: no relative drop at +20 sessions means drop the story.
